I can't confirm that for the whole period. The evidence is insufficient.

NASA FIRMS thermal detections (VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21 and MODIS) showed zero detections intersecting the asset from 2026-09-25 to 2026-10-24. The final day of the evaluated period, 2026-10-24 to 2026-10-25, isn't covered by any sensor. The latest near-real-time file update came before that day, so it was still in progress or not yet published.

Even for the covered days, "no detections" doesn't prove there was no fire. Small, short-lived, cool or cloud-obscured fires can go undetected. The data also says nothing about burned area or about anything outside the period.

In short, no thermal detections were found on the asset for about 30 of the 31 days, but the last day is unchecked. Re-running the check once the data for that day is published would close the gap.
